name: Aware Recovery Care
one_liner: In-home addiction treatment: a clinical team visits you at home for about a year, with medication if needed. Now run by Renew Health + Recovery.
best_for: Adults with alcohol or drug addiction who want treatment at home instead of a facility
People who need more support than weekly outpatient care
Families who want to take part in a loved one's treatment
People with commercial insurance in Renew's 11 states
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose: call 911, or call or text 988
People who need medically supervised detox or residential care
People with Medicaid or Medicare (reported as not accepted)
short_description: Insurance-paid in-home addiction treatment with a clinical team and family involvement, in 11 states; now operating as Renew Health + Recovery.
long_description: Aware Recovery Care started the in-home addiction treatment model, in which a care team (clinicians, nurses, recovery coaches and a care coordinator) treats alcohol and drug use at home over a long program, involves the family, and adds medication for addiction where appropriate. In September 2026 ARC Investco, doing business as Renew Health + Recovery, bought substantially all of Aware's assets; Aware's CEO stayed on, and the website now carries the Renew name. Trade press reported that Aware had been evicted from its Wallingford, Connecticut headquarters and faced a wage-and-hour lawsuit before the sale. Renew lists Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Maine, Rhode Island, Florida, Georgia, Virginia, Indiana, Kentucky and Ohio. It is in network with several commercial insurers (including many Anthem and Blue Cross Blue Shield plans); a treatment directory says it does not take Medicaid or Medicare. The company publishes its own outcome figures (such as abstinence and reduced ER use), but no peer-reviewed study of the program was found.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; no self-pay price published
pricing.notes: Check coverage by state and insurer on the vendor site or by phone. In network with several commercial plans (many Anthem and Blue Cross Blue Shield plans). A treatment directory reports no Medicaid or Medicare and lists an estimated cash price of about $4,340/month (third-party estimate, not from the vendor).

privacy.notes: Website policy says it will not distribute personal information to outside parties without consent, except vendors and legal requests; treatment records fall under HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2. No deletion right stated.

seo.meta_description: Aware Recovery Care provides in-home addiction treatment combining medication-assisted treatment with intensive clinical support, covered by most insurance.

faqs.q: How does in-home addiction treatment work?
faqs.a: Aware Recovery Care brings clinical staff to your home multiple times per week. You receive MAT medication management, individual and family therapy, case management, and 24/7 crisis support. Treatment intensity is similar to intensive outpatient but happens in your home rather than a clinic.

faqs.q: Does insurance cover Aware Recovery Care?
faqs.a: Yes, Aware accepts most major commercial insurance and Medicaid in many states. The in-home model is typically covered at similar rates to intensive outpatient treatment. Contact them to verify your specific insurance coverage.

faqs.q: How is Aware different from outpatient MAT?
faqs.a: Standard outpatient MAT involves clinic visits for medication and occasional therapy. Aware provides intensive support in your home with multiple weekly visits, family therapy, case management, and 24/7 access to clinical staff. It's more comprehensive than typical outpatient.

faqs.q: Where is Aware Recovery Care available?
faqs.a: Aware operates in multiple states with in-home services. Coverage areas continue to expand. Contact them directly to confirm service availability in your location.

primary_uses: In-home treatment of alcohol and drug use disorders

patient_summary: You check your insurance by state, then a team of a clinician, nurse, recovery coach and care coordinator works with you and your family at home over about a year, with medication for addiction where appropriate. It is now run as Renew Health + Recovery and is paid for by commercial insurance; it does not take Medicaid or Medicare, according to a treatment directory.

availability.note: 11 states: CT, MA, NH, ME, RI, FL, GA, VA, IN, KY, OH. Assets bought by Renew Health + Recovery in Sept 2026; operating under the Renew name.
